evidence.note: First full-suite run followed by 'Results' then 'Show failing tests' — establishes the run→enumerate-failures→target pattern that recurs across the whole trajectory.

Repeated full-suite runs each followed by 'Results' and 'Show all failing'/'Failing list'/'Test count', re-checking the entire surface after each fix cluster to catch regressions and see done-vs-remaining.
'Test results before changes' — captures a baseline before a risky edit, showing deliberate regression-guarding rather than reactive fixing.
Extended error-boundary debugging where it isolates the failure with node-level probes and dev-log inspection instead of blindly re-running, then returns to the full suite (898-903).
Cookie-writes subsystem worked through many isolated probes and repeated full-suite runs; shows sustained tracking of one pending area to completion late in the run.
TodoWrite used only a handful of times — planning ledger is light; the run/failing-list test cycle, not a structured per-area board, is the main progress-tracking device.

reasoning: The agent consistently runs the full 335-test suite after each fix cluster and enumerates the failing set and counts, giving it an accurate, continually refreshed done-vs-remaining picture and surfacing regressions across the whole surface — comfortably meeting anchor 5 and reaching toward 8 via its baseline-before-change check (712) and its habit of isolating stubborn failures with targeted probes rather than blind retries (803-896, 1116-1200). It falls short of 8-10 because tracking is driven by re-running everything rather than a maintained per-area pass-rate model, and the action index gives no explicit evidence of quantified area-by-area progress or self-declared loop-recognition.
